text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Finland will pay off a record 30 billion markka in state foreign currency debts this year; lending emphasis has moved from abroad to domestic market.
- Insurance fund managers would allow freer competition between pension funds as OECD proposed in its country report.
- The Forest Industry Federation and Paper Workers' Union start talks on Wednesday hoping to achieve agreement in dispute over Paper Workers' quitting collective pay talks.

- Proposed budget cuts would erode employment, Confederation of Union for Academic Professional (AKAVA), Confederation of Salaried Employees (STTK) and Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unions (SAK) say.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Demand for consumer loans will increase about 10 percent this year, banking sector says.

- Major customers of state-owned power company IVO and oil group Neste say they do not object to a possible merger, but state should listen to companies using gas and ensure competitive status for gas also, securing energy policy.
- Interest in foreign securities has doubled in a year: at the start of summer Finns 50 billion markka worth.
AAMULEHTI

- Employment policy sould be broadly renewed, social democrats urge at their party conference. Employment Minister, socialist MP Liisa Jaakonsaari proposes more services in employment offices and training in job hunting.
- Disputes on two billion markka of budget cuts are left to government budget discussions, Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto says. Most disagreements regard planned employment funds.
- Statistical correction of 1996 state deficit was not caused by a failure, but Statistics Finland did not have all information when counting, Finance Ministry says.
TURUN SANOMAT

- A possible merger between IVO and Neste would be mainly formed on the strategic aim of IVO to enlarge electricity markets: Neste would have to change its vision, says Kimmo Sasi, conservative MP and chairman of IVO supervisory board.
- Social democrats support consitutional committee's proposal to limit president powers.
- Energy and environmental taxes should be increased and job-related taxes cut by a billion markka, Green Party proposes.
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- Decision on a possible merger between Neste and IVO will not be forced, but made in democratic order, Trade and Industry Minister Antti Kalliomaki says.
- United Nations secretary general Kofi Annan and his wife arrive on Tuesday for a three-day official visit.
-- Nora Hallberg, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 292
